# OSS Knowledge Base Update Proposal: `golang.org/x/net`

Based on review of 11 unique vulnerabilities (deduplicated from 19 OSV/GHSA/GO entries), here are the proposed evidence-backed KB updates organized by affected subpackage.

---

## 1. `golang.org/x/net/http2` — HTTP/2 Protocol Vulnerabilities

### CVE-2022-27664 — HTTP/2 Connection Hang on Shutdown (DoS)
- **GHSA:** GHSA-69cg-p879-7622 | **GO:** GO-2022-0969
- **Impact:** Denial of service. HTTP/2 server connections hang forever if clean shutdown is preempted by a fatal error; exploitable by malicious clients.
- **Fix:** [CL 428735](https://go.dev/cl/428735) | [Issue 54658](https://go.dev/issue/54658)

### CVE-2022-41717 — Excessive Memory Growth via Large Header Keys
- **GHSA:** GHSA-xrjj-mj9h-534m | **GO:** GO-2022-1144
- **Impact:** ~64 MiB memory allocation per open connection. Header key cache is entry-count-capped but not size-capped.
- **Fix:** [CL 455717](https://go.dev/cl/455717), [CL 455635](https://go.dev/cl/455635) | [Issue 56350](https://go.dev/issue/56350)

### CVE-2022-41723 — HPACK Decoder CPU Exhaustion (DoS)
- **GHSA:** GHSA-vvpx-j8f3-3w6h | **GO:** GO-2023-1571
- **Impact:** Maliciously crafted HTTP/2 stream causes excessive CPU consumption in HPACK decoder; small number of small requests sufficient for DoS.
- **Fix:** [CL 468135](https://go.dev/cl/468135), [CL 468295](https://go.dev/cl/468295) | [Issue 57855](https://go.dev/issue/57855)

### CVE-2023-39325 — HTTP/2 Rapid Reset (DoS)
- **GHSA:** GHSA-4374-p667-p6c8 | **GO:** GO-2023-2102
- **Impact:** Clients rapidly creating and resetting streams bypass `MaxConcurrentStreams`, causing excessive server resource consumption. Related to industry-wide HTTP/2 Rapid Reset attack.
- **Fix:** Handler goroutines now bounded to stream concurrency limit; excess requests queued or connection terminated. [CL 534215](https://go.dev/cl/534215), [CL 534235](https://go.dev/cl/534235) | [Issue 63417](https://go.dev/issue/63417)

### CVE-2023-45288 — HTTP/2 CONTINUATION Flood (DoS)
- **GHSA:** GHSA-4v7x-pqxf-cx7m | **GO:** GO-2024-2687
- **Impact:** Excessive CONTINUATION frames force parsing of arbitrary header data (including Huffman-encoded data) even when headers exceed `MaxHeaderBytes`, causing CPU/memory exhaustion.
- **Fix:** Limit on excess header frames before connection closure. [CL 576155](https://go.dev/cl/576155) | [Issue 65051](https://go.dev/issue/65051)

---

## 2. `golang.org/x/net/http2/h2c` — Request Smuggling

### CVE-2022-41721 — Request Smuggling via MaxBytesHandler
- **GHSA:** GHSA-fxg5-wq6x-vr4w | **GO:** GO-2023-1495
- **Impact:** When `MaxBytesHandler` is used, unconsumed HTTP request body is misinterpreted as HTTP/2 frames, enabling request smuggling with attacker-crafted payloads.
- **Fix:** [CL 447396](https://go.dev/cl/447396) | [Issue 56352](https://go.dev/issue/56352)

---

## 3. `golang.org/x/net/html` — HTML Parsing / XSS Vulnerabilities

### CVE-2023-3978 — XSS via Improper Text Node Rendering
- **GHSA:** GHSA-2wrh-6pvc-2jm9 | **GO:** GO-2023-1988
- **Impact:** Text nodes outside the HTML namespace rendered literally without escaping, enabling cross-site scripting.
- **Fix:** [CL 514896](https://go.dev/cl/514896) | [Issue 61615](https://go.dev/issue/61615)
